title: How Willie Lynch's band became Irving Mills's Blue Rhythm Band
summary: Mills put Ellington and then Calloway into the Cotton Club, then used Lynch's band as a substitute and renamed Lynch Earl Jackson to keep 'royal' names.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Because you played with Joe Steele at the Savoy Ballroom.
I worked with him. Yes, I did.
Because he was in Willie Lynch's band, right?
And that later on became the Mills Blue Rhythm Band.
Now, you mentioned that Willie Lynch was a good friend of Irving Mills'.

When they wanted to... See, Irving Mills put Duke Ellington's band in the Cotton Club. Then when Duke come out to go on the road, he put Cab Calloway's band there. And both of them were so successful in the Cotton Club, when both of them come and was on the road, then Irving Mills got an idea that he would put another band in the Cotton Club in Cab Calloway's place, and that's where

Willie Lynch got the band together for Irving Mills -- and they called it the Blue Rhythm Band, Irving Mills' Blue Rhythm Band. And Willie Lynch was the leader, but they called him...his name was automatically changed to Earl Jackson, to keep the royal names up -- Count Basie, Duke Ellington, Earl Jackson. They were all royal names. Earl Hines and so forth, you know?
Which was nothing but the Mills Blue Rhythm Band when they recorded. You were on that session.
Well, Mills Blue Rhythm Band, let me see. When I was there, we didn't have no royal leader. The leader was either...
Either Carroll Dickerson... I'm trying to think of some of the leaders that used to be there... Carroll Dickerson. Sonny... Sonny something. And there was...
